\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Shocks (a), (b) and (c) of Table A18; annual panel 1996--2023, country and year fixed effects, two lags of the shock and of growth. Wage-bill response: change in the wage bill (\% of GDP) from t $-$ 2 to t + h on shock (a), dated t $-$ 1; Driscoll-Kraay 95\% CI. Multiplier: cumulative change in log real GDP per capita ($\times$100, from t $-$ 1, summed over horizons 0 to h) on the cumulative change in the wage bill (points of GDP, from t $-$ 2 for shock (a) and from t $-$ 1 for shocks (b) and (c), summed over 0 to h), instrumented by the shock (LP-IV, Ramey and Zubairy, 2018); Driscoll-Kraay standard errors (bandwidth 4) and normal 95\% CI; shock (b) is a generated regressor and its CIs are percentiles of a country block bootstrap that redoes the purge (999 replications; its standard error is the interquartile range of the bootstrap draws divided by 1.349, because draws with a near-zero first stage produce extreme ratios). F: Kleibergen-Paap robust first-stage F (one instrument); values below 10 indicate a weak instrument, and the multipliers and their CIs are then unreliable. θ/5: coefficient of the change in log GDP per capita ($\times$100) from t $-$ 1 to t + 5 on the mean change of the wage bill over h = 0--5, instrumented by the shock, divided by 5 (delta-method CI); dividing by 6, the number of growth years, gives values five-sixths as large. T3: the five-year coefficient ($-$0.142) and its 90\% CI. Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the second plan addendum).\end{minipage}
